They have learned to get all information on life from the internet and from watching videos, seeing articles on social media etc and assuming that the information they are being presented is true. They don't take the time to fact check themselves or the information that is being given to them and therefore begin to adopt beliefs that are not true and do not actually represent accurate depictions of certain events. 
[5.0_con] Social media aids in the formal conversation and discussion of varying ideas and topics. In this case, social media has made people smarter because they are willing to challenge the typical ways of communicating and job searching and stand by the millions of dollars they have made as they continue to do so.
[5.0_pro] If we were to actually gather data, I don't think it would support the argument that social media has made people smarter. I think we would find out that people all too frequently are taking things they see on social media as the truth and therefore they are being fed misinformation from multiple different angles. They take "influencers" for example and assume that because they have some level of popularity that they must know what they are talking about and are telling people the truth. They themselves start to spread this information to others and wind up making the masses less intelligent on the whole than they were before.
[5.0_con] In my closing argument, I would certainly like to stress the fact that while what we see on social media might appear alien or abnormal, it is certainly worth noting that it now has become trendy and is taking over as a whole because the lifestyle and glamour that it provides is not out of reach any longer. The walls and odds might be stacked against someone who did not go to school or who does not have wealthy parental figures. With the invention of social media, everyone not only has an equal chance at life and accomplishing their natural talents, but those high walls are now taken down as the playing field is now level and even. Social media is now becoming reality whereas before it was only a small reflection of it. 
[5.0_pro] I stand by my position that misinformation is being spread rampantly, whether intentionally or just purely through ignorance. Too often people just don't know any better and will spread things they see via social media to others on the assumption that because their friend/family member saw it and posted it, that it must be true. We need people to think for themselves and take the time to go through the information they are being fed and actually did into what is true. Social media is often not the real world and doesn't always give an accurate depiction of what the real world is actually like or what is actually going on. News and information spread easier because of social media, but if what is being spread isn't accurate or useful, you would have a hard time convincing me that people are suddenly smarter because of something they saw from a 12 year old on Tik Tok
